class LIS3DH_Simulator(BaseVirtualSensor):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        # Initialize all registers to their reset values
        self.regs = {
            0x0F: 0x33,  # WHO_AM_I
            0x1E: 0x10,  # CTRL_REG0
            0x1F: 0x00,  # TEMP_CFG_REG
            0x20: 0x07,  # CTRL_REG1
            0x23: 0x00,  # CTRL_REG4
            0x27: 0x00,  # STATUS_REG
            0x28: 0x00,  # OUT_X_L
            0x29: 0x00,  # OUT_X_H
            0x2A: 0x00,  # OUT_Y_L
            0x2B: 0x00,  # OUT_Y_H
            0x2C: 0x00,  # OUT_Z_L
            0x2D: 0x00   # OUT_Z_H
        }

    def read_register(self, addr: int, nbytes: int = 2) -> int:
        if addr not in self.regs:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid register address: {addr}")
        
        # Return the entire register value if nbytes is 2
        if nbytes == 2:
            return self.regs[addr]
        
        # For 1-byte reads, return only the relevant bits
        if addr in [0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2C, 0x2D]:
            return self.regs[addr] & 0xFF
        
        raise ValueError("Unsupported nbytes for single-byte read")

    def write_register(self, addr: int, data: int, nbytes: int = 2) -> None:
        if addr not in self.regs:
            raise ValueError(f"Invalid register address: {addr}")
        
        # Write to the entire register if nbytes is 2
        if nbytes == 2:
            self.regs[addr] = data
            return
        
        # For 1-byte writes, update only the relevant bits
        if addr in [0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2C, 0x2D]:
            self.regs[addr] &= ~0xFF  # Clear existing bits
            self.regs[addr] |= (data & 0xFF)  # Set new bits
            return
        
        raise ValueError("Unsupported nbytes for single-byte write")

from base_sensor import BaseVirtualSensor

class LIS3DH_Simulator(BaseVirtualSensor):
    def __init__(self):
        # Initialize all registers to their reset values
        self.regs = {
            0x0F: 0x33,  # WHO_AM_I
            0x1E: 0x10,  # CTRL_REG0
            0x1F: 0x00,  # TEMP_CFG_REG
            0x20: 0x07,  # CTRL_REG1
            0x23: 0x00,  # CTRL_REG4
            0x27: 0x00,  # STATUS_REG
            0x28: 0x00,  # OUT_X_L
            0x29: 0x00,  # OUT_X_H
            0x2A: 0x00,  # OUT_Y_L
            0x2B: 0x00,  # OUT_Y_H
            0x2C: 0x00,  # OUT_Z_L
            0x2D: 0x00   # OUT_Z_H
        }

    def read_register(self, addr: int, nbytes: int = 2) -> int:
        # Check if the address is within the valid range
        if addr not in self.regs:
            raise ValueError("Invalid register address")
        
        # Read the current value of the register
        value = self.regs[addr]
        
        # Handle single-byte access
        if nbytes == 1:
            # Return only the relevant bits based on the single_byte_semantics
            if addr in [0x28, 0x29, 0x2A, 0x2B, 0x2C, 0x2D]:
                return value & 0xFF
        
        return value

    def write_register(self, addr: int, data: int, nbytes: int = 2) -> None:
        # Check if the address is within the valid range
        if addr not in self.regs:
            raise ValueError("Invalid register address")
        
        # Write the data to the register
        self.regs[addr] = data
        
        # If the register is read-only, ignore the write
        if self.regs[addr] != data:
            raise ValueError("Attempted write to read-only register")
